judge.governing_law_identified: Conservation of volume fixes the merged-drop radius R=2^(1/3)a; the decrease in surface energy, kγ(A_initial-A_final), is converted into translational kinetic energy Mv^2/2.
judge.regime_assumed: Drops are spherical before and after merger, total water volume is conserved, surface energy is γ times the full spherical free-surface area, and the prescribed fraction k=0.06 of released surface energy becomes jump kinetic energy.

judge.governing_law_identified: Horizontal force balance on the cutout water block, with surface-tension forces acting tangentially at its left and right boundary edges.
judge.regime_assumed: Static equilibrium; uniform surface tension; forces evaluated per unit length along the y-axis.

judge.governing_law_identified: Hydrostatic pressure P=P0-rho g z combined with horizontal force balance between pressure forces and the horizontal components of surface tension on an arbitrary surface segment.
judge.regime_assumed: Static two-dimensional meniscus; constant density, uniform surface tension, uniform gravity, and a flat vertical board of negligible thickness. No small-slope approximation is used in this sub-part.

judge.governing_law_identified: Small-slope expansion of the capillary first integral from B.4, followed by the linear capillary equation z'' = z/ell^2.
judge.regime_assumed: |z'(x)| << 1, so cos(theta) = 1/sqrt(1+z'^2) is expanded as 1 - z'^2/2; the far-field surface is horizontal with z(infinity)=0.
case_branches_found: The growing solution A exp(x/ell) is excluded for x >= 0 by z(infinity)=0.
The remaining decaying solution applies for either sign of tan(theta0), representing elevation or depression within the small-slope regime.

judge.governing_law_identified: Hydrostatic pressure combined with the capillary first integral (1/2)rho g z^2 + gamma cos(theta) = constant along each connected free-surface segment.
judge.regime_assumed: Static, two-dimensional cross-section; identical rods arranged symmetrically, so the interface slope at the midpoint is zero, while the exterior interface becomes horizontal with z -> 0 at infinity.
